title: Rajiv Menon KC
subtitle: Defence advocacy, jury independence and the contempt proceedings
summary: A dedicated record of Menon’s work and the proceedings arising from his Filton closing speech. Court decisions, the defence position and wider professional concerns are kept distinct.
scope: A public-record profile, not a finding of professional misconduct. A procedural ruling, an allegation of contempt and a final determination are different things.
status_note: Latest judicial decision located in this review: 24 July 2026, ordering a stay pending jurisdictional and procedural challenges. Later professional commentary continues to describe unresolved proceedings. No final contempt judgment or later appeal outcome has been established here as of 19 October 2026.

sections.title: The advocate
sections.intro: Professional background from his chambers, separated from the disputed proceedings.

paragraphs.text: Rajiv Menon KC is a barrister at Garden Court Chambers. Its biography records his call to the Bar in 1993 and appointment as Queen’s Counsel in 2011. His work includes criminal trials and appeals, inquests, public inquiries and cases involving protest and state power.

The biography lists work on the Stephen Lawrence Inquiry, Hillsborough Inquests, Grenfell Tower Inquiry and UK Covid-19 Inquiry. These are professional instructions, not an endorsement by those inquiries of every position he has advanced.

sections.title: The proceedings, step by step
sections.intro: The jurisdiction of a court to hear an allegation must not be confused with whether the allegation is proved.

paragraphs.text: Menon represented Charlotte Head in the Filton trial at Woolwich Crown Court. Mr Justice Johnson considered that the closing speech breached directions concerning jury equity and other matters. Menon disputes the accusation. The resulting proceedings concern his advocacy, not an allegation that he participated in the underlying factory action.

sources.locator: Account of the allegation and denial

entries.title: 12 May 2026 · the first referral cannot proceed by that route
entries.citation: Re contempt proceedings against Rajiv Menon KC [2026] EWCA Civ 573

paragraphs.text: The Civil Division’s decision concerned the route by which the Crown Court had referred the matter to the High Court. The July judgment explains the result: the matter was left with the trial judge to consider other available steps, including referral to the Attorney General, the Bar Standards Board, or another High Court judge sitting in the Crown Court. This was not a final acquittal on the contempt allegation.

On 22 June, Johnson found a case to answer and considered proceedings to be in the public interest, while recognising the importance of uninhibited defence advocacy. He directed referral to a Presiding Judge to decide whether proceedings should be instituted and assigned to another judge. A case-to-answer finding is not a final determination of contempt.

sources.locator: Case to answer, public interest and procedure

paragraphs.text: The July judgment records that, on 29 June, Mr Justice Nicklin directed summary contempt proceedings and a summons for a hearing before Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb on 28 July. That listing was subsequently affected by the appeal decision below.

entries.title: 24 July 2026 · stay pending further challenges
entries.citation: Re Rajiv Menon KC [2026] EWCA Crim 966

paragraphs.text: Males LJ and Cutts J allowed an appeal against the refusal to vacate the hearing and ordered a stay of the proceedings before Cheema-Grubb J. They left the existing appeal to address Menon’s jurisdictional and procedural challenges. They did not decide those challenges or the merits of the contempt allegation.

sections.title: Judicial authority and independent advocacy
sections.intro: Competing concerns deserve to be stated accurately, without turning either side’s argument into a finding.

paragraphs.text: Johnson’s ruling stresses compliance with legal directions and the administration of justice. It treats the alleged conduct as more than a single isolated remark. The issue is therefore not captured completely by saying a lawyer was prosecuted merely for representing an unpopular client.

entries.title: The concern about a chilling effect

paragraphs.text: Garden Court Chambers argues that the proceedings could inhibit lawyers’ ability to defend clients fearlessly. Raj Chada’s Legal Action commentary frames the dispute as one about the balance between judicial authority and defence independence, and records Menon’s denial. These are attributed professional views, not a court’s resolution of that balance.

sections.title: What would update this page?
sections.intro: A dated research record, not an automated live court feed.

paragraphs.text: The next decisive documents would be a judgment on the outstanding jurisdictional appeal, an order changing the stay, or a final contempt decision. None has been located in this review. A planned hearing or public meeting is not evidence that a hearing took place or that an allegation was proved.

Garden Court maintains a dedicated page linking judgments, the closing-speech transcript and professional responses. It is a useful source index from Menon’s chambers, rather than an independent adjudication of his case.
